note: Adapted from Snyder 1922, original in English (Proceedings of the United States National Museum 61, Art. 20). The original name is Kalotermes cubanus, now placed in Neotermes. Type locality Cuba: Pinar del Rio: Las Playuelas; described from a large series of soldiers collected at the type locality by D. T. Barreto in January 1921 (month 1) (collection No. 5616, OCR'd as SG1G), the holotype soldier in the U.S.N.M., catalogue No. 24565. The original describes the soldier only; the alate is unknown (the author suggested that the soldier of this species may correspond to the alate of K. montanus Snyder). The measurement item 'head without mandibles and labrum' appears in the OCR as lalmim and has been read from the context; the figures of the postmentum and of the hind femur (figs. 1–2) have not been translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This species is close to Kalotermes jouteli Banks of Florida and K. mona Banks of Mona Island in the Antilles, but differs clearly in structure, most conspicuously in the broad mandibles; the antennae of K. mona have a longer third segment. Compared with K. jouteli, this species has smaller eye spots and paler pigmentation, and the postmentum (gula) is much narrower in the middle, its middle width less than half its anterior width.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown, darker in front (especially on the frons) and paler behind; head twice as long as wide, about equally wide at front and back, the sides slightly concave. Postclypeus chestnut, wider than long, its posterior margin convex. Labrum yellowish brown, wider than long, broadly rounded at the tip, with long hairs. The dorsal and ventral surfaces of the head bear scattered long straight erect hairs. Eye spot much smaller than in Kalotermes jouteli and paler, situated at the level of the antennal socket and close to it. Mandibles black, stout, very broad at the base; the left mandible with 2 pointed marginal teeth near the tip, the proximal one wider; the right mandible with 2 wider and larger pointed teeth below the marginal teeth of the left mandible; the tips of the mandibles pointed and curved inward. Antennae yellowish brown, the first 3 segments chestnut, 17-segmented, longer than the mandibles, covered with long pubescence; segment 3 larger than segment 2 and than segment 4, club-shaped, dark; the terminal segment short and slender, nearly oval. Postmentum very narrow in the middle, its middle width less than half its anterior width (original fig. 1). Pronotum yellowish brown with a dark border along the anterior margin, its median width slightly less than twice its length, wider than the head; the anterior margin arcuately concave, the widest point near the front, the anterior margin raised at the corners; the sides rounded, narrowing toward the rear; the posterior margin nearly straight; the margin of the pronotum with long hairs. Abdomen similar in colour to the pronotum, paler beneath, covered with short pale pubescence. Legs paler, the tibiae and tarsi darker, the femora extremely swollen (original fig. 2). Measurements: soldier total length 13.5 mm; head with mandibles 5.75 mm; head length (excluding mandibles and labrum) 3.80 mm; left mandible length 1.90 mm; pronotum length 1.80 mm; hind tibia length 1.80 mm; head width 2.75 mm; pronotum width 3.00 mm.
